title: Grade 9 Science — Motion & Force and Laws of Motion
description: Motion and Force and Laws of Motion practice questions
subject: science

questions.question: A body is said to be in motion when:
options: It is at rest with respect to all objects
Its position changes with respect to a reference point over time
It is acted upon by a force
questions.explanation: Motion is the change in position of an object with respect to a reference point (observer) over time. Rest and motion are relative concepts.

questions.question: The SI unit of speed is:
questions.explanation: The SI (International System) unit of speed is metres per second (m/s). While km/h is commonly used, m/s is the standard scientific unit.

questions.question: A car travels 60 km in 2 hours. Its average speed is:
questions.explanation: Average speed = Total distance / Total time = 60 km / 2 h = 30 km/h.

questions.question: The slope of a velocity-time graph gives:
questions.explanation: Slope = change in velocity / change in time = acceleration. On a v-t graph, the slope represents acceleration.

questions.question: A ball is thrown vertically upward with velocity 20 m/s (g = 10 m/s²). The time taken to reach the highest point is:
questions.explanation: At the highest point, final velocity v = 0. Using v = u + at: 0 = 20 + (−10)t → t = 2 s.

questions.question: The area under a velocity-time graph gives:
questions.explanation: Area under a v-t graph = velocity × time = displacement. This gives the total displacement covered during the time interval.

questions.question: A car starts from rest and accelerates uniformly at 2 m/s². Its velocity after 5 seconds is:
A body moves in a circular path at constant speed. Its motion is called:
questions.explanation: Uniform circular motion: constant speed but continuously changing direction. Since direction changes, velocity changes — so there IS acceleration (centripetal), even though speed is constant.

questions.question: Newton's first law of motion is also called the law of:
questions.explanation: Newton's first law states that a body continues in its state of rest or uniform motion unless acted upon by an external force. This property is called inertia.

questions.question: The SI unit of force is:
questions.explanation: The SI unit of force is the Newton (N). 1 N = 1 kg·m/s². It is named after Sir Isaac Newton.

questions.question: According to Newton's second law, force F = ma. If mass is doubled and acceleration is halved, the force becomes:
questions.explanation: F = ma. New force = (2m)(a/2) = ma = F. The force remains the same.

questions.question: Newton's third law states: 'For every action, there is an equal and opposite ___.'
questions.explanation: Newton's third law: For every action (force), there is an equal and opposite reaction. Both forces act on different objects simultaneously.

questions.question: A rocket moves forward because:
options: Exhaust gases push the rocket forward
By Newton's third law, exhaust gases expelled backward push the rocket forward
Newton's first law keeps it moving
questions.explanation: By Newton's third law, when the rocket expels gases backward (action), the gases exert an equal and opposite forward force on the rocket (reaction). This propels the rocket.

questions.question: The momentum of a body of mass 5 kg moving at 10 m/s is:
questions.explanation: Momentum p = mass × velocity = 5 kg × 10 m/s = 50 kg·m/s.

questions.question: The law of conservation of momentum states that the total momentum of a system remains constant if:
options: No external force acts on the system
Objects move in the same direction
All objects have the same mass
questions.explanation: Conservation of momentum: in the absence of an external force, the total momentum of a system remains constant. Internal forces within the system don't change total momentum.
